name: bumpsmith

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.description: Repositories you can use with the other tools.

tools.name: scan_dependencies
tools.description: List the repository's direct dependencies that are one or more major versions behind, with the latest version and whether it has passed the release-age wait. No AI; only package names are looked up on the public registry.

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

tools.name: check_release
tools.description: Is this version safe to adopt? Reports publish age, yanked and deprecated status, and whether OSV lists it as malicious, against Bumpsmith's release gate (3-day minimum age by default). No AI.

min_age_days.description: Minimum release age in days (at least 3, as in the upgrade pipeline)

tools.name: api_diff
tools.description: Compare the TypeScript type definitions of two versions of an npm package: removed, added and changed exports. No AI. Useful to see exactly what a major version changed.

tools.name: explain_upgrade
tools.description: What breaks when this repository moves a direct dependency to a new version, and every place in the code that is affected. Reads the release notes, changelog and type definitions (uses the configured model; a few cents).

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

tools.name: start_upgrade
tools.description: Upgrade a dependency in an isolated sandbox, fix the code the upgrade breaks, verify with the repository's own checks before and after, and review the diff. Takes a few minutes and runs in the background: poll get_upgrade with the returned id. Nothing is written to the repository until apply_upgrade.

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

provider.description: Model provider (default: the configured one), e.g. anthropic-api, claude-code, codex, openai

tools.name: get_upgrade
tools.description: Status of a running upgrade (id from start_upgrade) or the result of a finished one (run id from list_upgrades): state, confidence, cost, the evidence (what changed upstream, what changed here, checks before and after, the review). States: "ready" (verified in the sandbox and approved by the independent review; safe to apply), "safe" (version bump only, checks pass), "needs_human" (could not prove the change; read the evidence), "blocked_policy" (refused: malicious, too new, or a safety rule), "failed_infra" (the sandbox could not run the repository).

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

tools.name: list_upgrades
tools.description: Recent upgrade runs in this repository, newest first, with their state.

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

tools.name: apply_upgrade
tools.description: Stage a finished upgrade's patch in the working tree (git apply --check, then git apply --index). Only "ready" and "safe" results apply; the user reviews with git diff --cached and commits.

repository.description: Path to the repository (default: the folder Bumpsmith was started in).

instructions:
Bumpsmith upgrades a dependency across a breaking change and proves it: it reads the release notes (every breaking change backed by a quote), finds the affected code, edits it in an isolated sandbox, runs the repository's own install/build/typecheck/lint/tests before and after, and has an independent reviewer check the diff.

Typical flow: check_release (is the version safe to adopt?) → explain_upgrade (what breaks, where) → start_upgrade → get_upgrade until it finishes → read the evidence → apply_upgrade only when the state is "ready" or "safe", and tell the user what changed. Never present a "needs_human" result as fixed. States: "ready" (verified in the sandbox and approved by the independent review; safe to apply), "safe" (version bump only, checks pass), "needs_human" (could not prove the change; read the evidence), "blocked_policy" (refused: malicious, too new, or a safety rule), "failed_infra" (the sandbox could not run the repository).
